newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks rise helped by banks, weaker yen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks rise helped by banks, weaker yen.

text.p: Tokyo stocks rose on Thursday morning, lifted by short-covering of banking sector issues and a weaker yen, which encouraged buying of some exporter issues, brokers said. However, they said eyes were still on currencies ahead of the Group of Seven (G7) summit next week.

The Nikkei 225 ended the morning up 216.82 points, or 1.07 percent, at 20,506.75. June futures were up 210 points at 20,520. "Some smaller high-techs and semiconductor issues gained momentum after the yen weakened to 112 to the dollar halfway through the session," said Noboru Yorita, general manager at Tachibana Securities.

"Non-life insurers and real estate issues have gained considerably recently compared to banks, and investors feel that there is a need to buy back the bank shares they sold off in past months and bring them up to similar levels," he added.
Turnover at the end of the two-hour session was 190 million shares, little changed from 189 million shares in the previous session. Gainers outdid losers 727 to 298, while 211 issues were unchanged.
Despite the buying seen in some high-tech issues, such as Advantest Corp, which jumped 250 yen to 8,550, investors steered away from car makers.
